content: 1. Administer 200 mg of fluconazole orally on Day 1, followed by 100 mg orally once daily. Doses up to 400 mg per day may be used depending on the patient’s response. 2. For suppression of relapse in patients with AIDS, administer 200 mg orally once daily. 3. For prevention of candidiasis in patients undergoing bone marrow transplantation, administer 400 mg orally once daily. 4. For uncomplicated infections, administer 150 mg orally as a single dose. For complicated infections, administer 150 mg orally every 72 hours for three doses. For recurrent infections, administer 150 mg orally once daily for 10–14 days, followed by 150 mg once weekly for six months. 5. In cases of hepatic impairment, fluconazole has not been adequately studied. 6. For esophageal candidiasis, administer 6 mg/kg orally on Day 1, followed by 3 mg/kg once daily. Doses up to 12 mg/kg/day may be used based on the patient’s response, but do not exceed 600 mg/day. 7. Fluconazole and alfuzosin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Fluconazole and asenapine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 9. Fluconazole and buprenorphine (long-acting injection) both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Fluconazole and ceritinib both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Fluconazole and citalopram both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 12. Fluconazole increases the levels of deuruxolitinib by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 13. Deuruxolitinib is contraindicated with strong or moderate CYP2C9 inhibitors. 14. Fluconazole and disopyramide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 15. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin base by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and co-administration is contraindicated. 16. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and co-administration is contraindicated. 17. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and co-administration is contraindicated. 19. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of flibanserin by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of severe hypotension or syncope. 20. Fluconazole and ibutilide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 21. Fluconazole and indapamide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 22. Fluconazole increases the levels of lomitapide by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as it significantly increases lomitapide levels. 23. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of lonafarnib by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated as lonafarnib is a sensitive CYP3A4 substrate. 24. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of mavacamten by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of heart failure caused by systolic dysfunction. 25. Fluconazole and pentamidine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Fluconazole and pimozide both prolong the QTc interval. Fluconazole also increases pimozide levels by reducing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated due to the risk of QT interval prolongation. 27. Fluconazole and procainamide both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of quinidine by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, and co-administration is contraindicated. 29. Ribociclib increases the toxicity of fluconazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 30. Fluconazole and solifenacin both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 31. Fluconazole and sunitinib both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 32. Fluconazole and tacrolimus both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration is contraindicated. 33. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of abrocitinib by inhibiting its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. Abrocitinib is a substrate of CYP2C9 and CYP2C19, and inhibitors of these enzymes increase its systemic exposure, potentially leading to adverse effects. 34. Fluconazole and adagrasib both prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, frequent monitoring is recommended due to the risk of torsades de pointes and other serious arrhythmias. 35. Fluconazole increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by inhibiting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs prolong the QTc interval. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug.
